svg.title: A Nested Cohort Behind the Base Revenue Target
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-nested-annual-recovery-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: A Nested Cohort Behind the Base Revenue Target; subtitle: 250 screened prospects become 25 earned-and-collected engagements; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative mature annual cohort, not measured conversion performance or a first-month forecast. Every downstream group is a subset of the preceding group. Twenty-five engagements at $20,200 average annual earned operator fees reconcile to $505,000 Base revenue; the average is a modeling input.; caption: Stage conversions are 40.0%, 60.0%, 66.7%, and 62.5%; overall conversion is 10.0%. Pending cases remain outside the final earned-and-collected cohort.; stages: label: Screened corporate prospects; value: 250 organizations with auditable recurring spend; numeric value: 250.0; detail: Identify organizations with accessible invoice history, a responsible account owner, and a plausible recovery lane. Exclude accounts already bound by conflicting recovery engagements before outreach.; label: Authorized client engagements; value: 100 signed engagements from those prospects; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Forty percent of screened prospects execute authority and scope documents and provide baseline records. A verbal expression of interest does not count as an authorized engagement.; label: Evidence-qualified recovery cases; value: 60 engagements with documented eligible opportunities; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Sixty percent of authorized engagements survive contract, deadline, statutory, and evidence checks. Remove duplicate recoveries, unsupported estimates, and claims barred by applicable waivers.; label: Accepted recovery submissions; value: 40 engagements reach accepted filing channels; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Two-thirds of qualified engagements obtain submission receipts or accepted processing records. Count client engagements consistently rather than inflating this stage with multiple invoices from one client.; label: Earned and collected engagements; value: 25 engagements generate $505,000 operator revenue; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Twenty-five engagements meet earning conditions and collection assumptions within the modeled year. $505,000 divided by 25 equals $20,200 per engagement; this is operator fee revenue, not client recovery principal or total underlying vendor expenditure.

text.title: A Nested Cohort Behind the Base Revenue Target
text.tspan: A Nested Cohort Behind the Base Revenue Target

rect.title: label: Screened corporate prospects; value: 250 organizations with auditable recurring spend; numeric value: 250.0; detail: Identify organizations with accessible invoice history, a responsible account owner, and a plausible recovery lane. Exclude accounts already bound by conflicting recovery engagements before outreach.

label: Authorized client engagements; value: 100 signed engagements from those prospects; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Forty percent of screened prospects execute authority and scope documents and provide baseline records. A verbal expression of interest does not count as an authorized engagement.

label: Evidence-qualified recovery cases; value: 60 engagements with documented eligible opportunities; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Sixty percent of authorized engagements survive contract, deadline, statutory, and evidence checks. Remove duplicate recoveries, unsupported estimates, and claims barred by applicable waivers.

label: Accepted recovery submissions; value: 40 engagements reach accepted filing channels; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Two-thirds of qualified engagements obtain submission receipts or accepted processing records. Count client engagements consistently rather than inflating this stage with multiple invoices from one client.

label: Earned and collected engagements; value: 25 engagements generate $505,000 operator revenue; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Twenty-five engagements meet earning conditions and collection assumptions within the modeled year. $505,000 divided by 25 equals $20,200 per engagement; this is operator fee revenue, not client recovery principal or total underlying vendor expenditure.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative mature annual cohort, not measured conversion performance or a first-month forecast. Every downstream group is a subset of the preceding group. Twenty-five engagements at $20,200 average annual earned operator fees reconcile to $505,000 Base revenue; the average is a modeling input.
